language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

<meta>Beijing Kanjur (1718–1720), Tantra section (秘密經 / Dandar-a), Volume 5 (第五卷 / ᢌᠠ), folio 150 recto (上一百五十 / ᠵᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠲᠠᠪᠢᠨ)</meta>
<margin>ᢌᠠ ᠲᠠᠪᠤ ᠵᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠲᠠᠪᠢᠨ</margin>

ᠬᠤᠪᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠁ ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ
ᠪᠤᠢ ᠁ ᠲᠡᠳᠡ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠁ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ
ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠄ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠬᠤ ᠳᠤ
ᠣᠨᠣᠭᠳᠠᠬᠤᠢ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠁ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠨᠢᠭᠤᠴᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ
ᠡᠷᠬᠡᠲᠦ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ ᠁ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠢᠨᠦ
ᠪᠦᠳᠦᠭᠦᠨ ᠁ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠄ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ ᠨᠠᠷᠢᠨ ᠪᠠ
ᠪᠦᠳᠦᠭᠦᠨ ᠁ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠥᠨᠳᠦᠷ ᠪᠠ ᠪᠣᠭᠣᠨᠢ ᠁
ᠬᠤᠪᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠨ ᠪᠠ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠥᠨᠳᠦᠷ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ
ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ᠄ ᠥᠨᠳᠦᠷ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠁
ᠥᠨᠳᠦᠷ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠳᠣᠷᠣᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠄ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ ᠣᠷᠣ ᠪᠠ ᠣᠷᠣ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ
ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠨ ᠣᠨᠣᠭᠳᠠᠬᠤᠢ ᠄ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠪᠣᠳᠢᠰᠠᠳᠣ ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ ᠁ ᠶᠠᠮᠪᠠᠷ ᠮᠡᠲᠦ
ᠲᠡᠮᠳᠡᠭ ᠪᠠ ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠶᠢ ᠁ ᠣᠨᠣᠭᠳᠠᠬᠤᠢ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠬᠤᠪᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ
ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠁ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠨ ᠥᠨᠳᠦᠷ ᠪᠠ
ᠪᠣᠭᠣᠨᠢ ᠁ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠥᠨᠳᠦᠷ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠄ ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠴᠠᠭ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄ ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠁ ᠳᠦᠷᠰᠦ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠦ
ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠪᠣᠳᠠᠲᠤ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠢᠨᠦ
ᠭᠠᠭᠴᠠ ᠁ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠄ ᠲᠡᠳᠡ ᠪᠠ
ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠁ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠪᠣᠳᠢᠰᠠᠳᠣ ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ ᠶᠠᠮᠪᠠᠷ
ᠭᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠄ ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠭᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ
ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠁ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠭᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠪᠣᠳᠠᠲᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄
ᠭᠠᠭᠴᠠ ᠮᠤᠲᠤᠷ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠁ ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠄ ᠣᠨᠣᠭᠳᠠᠬᠤᠢ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠪᠦᠳᠦᠭᠦᠨ ᠁ ᠬᠤᠪᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠭᠠᠨ ᠬᠡᠢ
ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠁ ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠁
ᠣᠨᠣᠭᠳᠠᠬᠤᠢ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠬᠤᠪᠢ ᠁ ᠬᠤᠪᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠨ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠬᠡᠢ ᠄ ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠰᠡᠳᠬᠢᠯ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ
ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ᠥᠨᠳᠦᠷ ᠪᠠ ᠪᠣᠭᠣᠨᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠁ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ
ᠪᠦᠳᠦᠭᠦᠨ ᠪᠠ ᠨᠠᠷᠢᠨ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠁ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠦ ᠪᠠ ᠰᠠᠢᠲᠤᠷ
ᠰᠡᠳᠬᠢᠯ ᠢ ᠣᠨᠣᠭᠳᠠᠬᠤᠢ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠁ ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ
ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ᠁ ᠬᠤᠪᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠢᠨᠦ ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠯ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ
<vocab>ᠨᠢᠭᠤᠴᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠡᠷᠬᠡᠲᠦ, ᠪᠣᠳᠢᠰᠠᠳᠣ, ᠭᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ, ᠮᠤᠲᠤᠷ, ᠢᠯᠡᠷᠬᠡᠢ, ᠪᠦᠳᠦᠭᠦᠨ, ᠨᠠᠷᠢᠨ, ᠬᠡᠢ, ᠰᠡᠳᠬᠢᠯ, 秘密經</vocab>

<meta>Beijing Kanjur, 1718 to 1720, Tantra section, Secret Scriptures, Volume 5, folio 150 recto; continues from previous page</meta>
<margin><term>Ca</term> <gloss>fifth volume</gloss>, five, one hundred fifty <note>original: "ᢌᠠ ᠲᠠᠪᠤ ᠵᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠲᠠᠪᠢᠨ"</note></margin>
<margin>Secret Scriptures, Volume Five, recto, one hundred fifty <note>original: "秘密經第五卷上一百五十"</note></margin>
the portion <note>original: "qubi", translating Sanskrit kalā or bhāga, a part or aspect</note> and the beyond <note>original: "činaγsi", translating Sanskrit para, the transcendent</note>, has taught the six distinctions.
As for all of those, the distinction of the beyond and the non-beyond
is to be understood when distinguishing by means of the six distinctions of the beyond.
As for the distinction of the six beyonds: herein, O Lord of
Secrets <term>niγuča-yin erketü</term> <gloss>Lord of Secrets, an epithet of Vajrapāṇi</gloss>, the beyond is manifest <term>ilerkei</term> <gloss>manifest, evident</gloss>; the non-beyond is
coarse <term>büdügün</term> <gloss>coarse, gross</gloss>; as for the beyond of the beyond, within that, moreover, are the subtle <term>narin</term> <gloss>subtle, fine</gloss> and
the coarse; the beyond and non-beyond is high and low;
and the portion as well as the non-beyond constitute the distinction of the non-high:
thus He spoke. The high is above;
the non-high is below. Within that, moreover, by the distinction of place and non-place <note>original: "oro ba oro busu", locus and non-locus</note>,
it is to be distinguished and understood. Therein, as for the <term>bodisado</term> <gloss>bodhisattvas, awakening beings</gloss>, how
the marks and signs are to be understood: therein, the distinction of the portion and the beyond,
the six distinctions of the beyond as well as the high and
the low, the non-beyond, the unmanifest, and the non-high. Those
that are beyond are timeless; the non-beyond of the unmanifest is formless; its
sign is the beyond of three realities <note>original: "γurban bodatu", the three substantial realities</note>, while the unmanifest non-beyond is
single. Of the manifest beyond that is not shown: those and
the six distinctions are the non-beyond. Therein, what are the
hand-signs <term>γar-un belge</term> <gloss>hand-signs, ritual gestures</gloss> of the bodhisattvas? As for the hand-sign of the non-beyond of the unmanifest,
the hand-sign of the beyond of the other is without substantial reality:
it is a single <term>mutur</term> <gloss>mudrā, ritual seal or hand gesture</gloss>. Of the unmanifest: the beyond
sign that is to be understood is coarse; rendered as the portion and the beyond, it is without
wind <term>kei</term> <gloss>wind, vital breath or prāṇa</gloss>: it is the non-beyond. Of the unmanifest,
the beyond and non-beyond that is to be understood is the portion; the portion and
the beyond is the wind; the unmanifest is the mind <term>sedkil</term> <gloss>mind, consciousness</gloss>: thus
He spoke. As for the distinction of high and low, and therein, moreover,
the distinction of coarse and subtle, of that too the mind
is to be thoroughly understood. It is the unmanifest beyond: thus

<summary>This folio from the fifth volume of the Tantra section of the Beijing Kanjur presents a Buddhist tantric discourse addressed to the Lord of Secrets, Vajrapāṇi, and the bodhisattvas. It classifies the sixfold distinctions of the transcendent beyond and the non-beyond in relation to manifest and unmanifest states, coarse and subtle levels, ritual hand-signs, vital wind, and mind.</summary>
<keywords>Beijing Kanjur, Tantra, Classical Mongolian, Lord of Secrets, Vajrapani, bodhisattva, mudra, hand-sign, manifest and unmanifest, coarse and subtle, vital wind, mind</keywords>
